description:
The historic Château du Breuil brings together an 18th-century château, former farm buildings and an old-style wine cellar with the new timber houses of the Hameau du Marais, all spread across 110 acres (45 hectares) of private forest in the heart of the Loire Valley. Twenty years after opening Les Sources de Caudalie in the Bordeaux vineyards, Alice and Jérôme Tourbier opened Les Sources de Cheverny. Just ten minutes away, the internationally famous Château de Cheverny has belonged to the same family for more than six centuries.

Today its 49 rooms are spread between the original 18th-century château, restored stone farm buildings, and new Scandinavian-style lakeside cabins (the Hameau du Marais). Categories range from Superior to Deluxe, Junior Suite and Suite.

The Tourbiers' prior track record with Les Sources de Caudalie, opened two decades earlier in Bordeaux's wine country, ties this property to an established formula of pairing historic estates with contemporary spa hospitality.

The resort's mix of an original manor château, restored agricultural outbuildings, and entirely new lakeside cabin construction gives Les Sources de Cheverny one of the most architecturally varied room inventories among the France collection's château-hotels.

The property's position ten minutes from Château de Cheverny — the real-life inspiration for Marlinspike Hall in the Tintin comics, in the same family for over six centuries — gives guests staying here easy access to one of the Loire Valley's most visited and longest continuously family-owned châteaux.
history: Les Sources de Cheverny combines the historic 18th-century Château du Breuil, restored farm buildings and an old wine cellar with the new timber Hameau du Marais, across 45 hectares of private forest. It was opened by Alice and Jérôme Tourbier, twenty years after they opened Les Sources de Caudalie in Bordeaux's vineyards. Its 49 rooms and suites are spread between the original château, restored stone farm buildings, and new lakeside Scandinavian-style cabins.

faqs.question: Are all the rooms at Les Sources de Cheverny within the original château?
faqs.answer: No — only some Junior Suites are in the original 18th-century château. Most of the 49 rooms are in restored stone farm buildings or new lakeside cabins (Hameau du Marais). Guests wanting the château experience specifically should book a Junior Suite in the historic building.

faqs.question: Who owns Les Sources de Cheverny?
faqs.answer: Alice and Jérôme Tourbier, who opened it twenty years after founding Les Sources de Caudalie in the Bordeaux vineyards.

faqs.question: How far is Les Sources de Cheverny from Château de Cheverny?
faqs.answer: About 10 minutes — Château de Cheverny, the real-life inspiration for Marlinspike Hall in Tintin, has belonged to the same family for over six centuries.

hotel.how_to_stay:
**Getting there:** 2 hours from Paris; 10 minutes from the famous Château de Cheverny, in the heart of the Loire Valley vineyards.

**Rooms & rates:** 49 rooms and suites spread between the 18th-century château, restored farm buildings, and new lakeside cabins, from about €250 to €500+ per night.

**On-site:** Caudalie spa, Michelin-starred restaurant, the estate's own vineyard (producing La Grand Vigne wine), 45 hectares of private forest.

**Good to know:** Only a portion of the 49 rooms are in the original manor-style château — most of the inventory is new Scandinavian-style cabins or restored farm buildings; guests wanting the château experience specifically should book a Junior Suite in the historic building.

**Combine with:** Château de Cheverny (10 min) — the real-life inspiration for Marlinspike Hall in Tintin.
